historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR, anchored on FY2027 guidance (flat) and segment guidance; equity CAGR rejected as distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable as a growth anchor in either window: the 5-year figure (12.0%) is inflated by the A$6.3bn equity raise that funded Vifor in FY2022, and the 3-year figure (-2.1%) is depressed by the US$7.1bn of FY2026 impairments. Both diverge by more than 30% from revenue and EPS.
historical_growth.notes: All figures from CSL.AX_Metrics.csv through FY2026. FY2026 endpoints: revenue 15,797; attributable equity 14,797; owner FCF 2,063. Owner FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, the group is in net debt): FY2021 1,863, FY2022 1,264, FY2023 770, FY2024 1,337, FY2025 2,414, FY2026 2,063. The 3-year FCF CAGR is flattered by a trough base (FY2023 capex of 1,692 during the Vifor integration); the 5-year figure of 2.1% against 8.9% revenue growth is the more honest read: Vifor added revenue, not cash per share. SBC grew from 92 to 172 over the five years (13% a year), faster than revenue, but is only 1.1% of revenue. EPS CAGRs use FY2026 UNDERLYING NPAT per share of US$5.89 (underlying NPATA attributable 3,098 less acquired-IP amortisation attributable 261 = 2,837, over 481.98m weighted shares; FY2026 annual segment reconciliation) against statutory EPS of 4.53 (FY2023) and 5.21 (FY2021), because FY2026 statutory EPS is a loss of US$5.35 and no CAGR exists on it. On underlying NPATA per share (6.43 against 6.65 in FY2025) earnings fell 3%.

scenario_narratives.base: The reset holds and CSL becomes a mid-single-digit grower again. FY2027 lands on guidance: flat revenue as Behring's mid-single-digit growth and Andembry's ramp are cancelled by a 25% fall at Vifor (generic iron, the end of Velphoro's TDAPA period, Tavneos withdrawn). From FY2028 Behring carries the group at 4-5%, in line with an immunoglobulin market growing mid-to-high single digits, less continued albumin weakness in China and the Medicaid pricing concessions. The EBITDA margin rises about two points to 35.5% on the cost program and a modest Behring gross-margin recovery, but does not regain the 36% of FY2021 because Vifor's highest-margin revenue is gone and half the savings are reinvested. Capex stays above 8% of revenue through the Kankakee build before easing.
scenario_narratives.bull: Behring's gross margin, stuck near 50% since the pandemic against 57% for the group before it, finally recovers as plasma cost per litre falls (the Haemonetics platform rollout by end-2027, Horizon 2 yield gains once the clinical evidence is in) and immunoglobulin grows at the top of the market range. Andembry and Hemgenix become billion-dollar products, Vifor stabilises on nephrology after FY2027, and the new chief executive delivers the full savings program. Revenue compounds at 5-7% and the EBITDA margin reaches 38%. This needs several independent things to go right, and Horizon 2 has already been delayed once.
scenario_narratives.bear: Immunoglobulin, 40% of revenue, loses its pricing power and some of its volume: FcRn inhibitors take share in CIDP and myasthenia gravis, Medicare Part D redesign and most-favoured-nation Medicaid pricing compress US net price, and China's albumin cost containment persists. Generic competition spreads from Venofer to Ferinject so Vifor keeps shrinking after FY2027, US influenza vaccination keeps declining, and the leadership transition and class action distract from the cost program. Revenue falls in FY2027, stalls in FY2028 and then grows only 2.5-3%; the margin slips to 31% while the US manufacturing build still has to be paid for.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CSL is valued on unlevered owner free cash flow in US dollars: underlying EBITDA before share-based pay, less share-based pay and the full lease cost, taxed on an unlevered basis, less all capex including licence and IP payments, less the working capital that plasma inventory absorbs as the business grows. Net debt excludes leases because they are charged in the flows; Fresenius's 45% of the renal joint venture, contingent consideration, the pension deficit and the remaining restructuring cash are deducted in the bridge. Per-share values are converted to Australian dollars at a dated rate for comparison with the ASX price. The FY2026 impairments are non-cash and are not in the flows, but they are evidence about the Vifor acquisition and they lower the margin and growth paths. The statutory FY2026 loss is not an earnings base; underlying NPATA of 3,098 is, and the year-1 flows tie to it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the enterprise value, so the result is sensitive to the 8.5% WACC; US rates are high (CSL's own 10-year paper priced at 6.2%) and a lower rate environment would lift every scenario.

The FY2027 profit guidance flatters the cash picture: much of the guided growth in underlying NPAT comes from lower amortisation of acquired IP after the write-downs and from cost savings, with revenue flat.

Working capital: receivables, inventories and payables absorbed about US$1.0bn in FY2026 on almost no revenue growth. The model charges working capital only on revenue growth, so year 1 (flat revenue) assumes no repeat; a repeat would cost about A$3 a share for each year it persisted.
Behring gross margin is the largest single swing factor between the scenarios and has disappointed for four years.
Immunoglobulin substitution by FcRn inhibitors and US net-price pressure sit in the bear case only.
The class action filed in October 2026 is unquantified and is not in the bridge.
The Metrics CSV EBITDA for FY2026 (-2,641) includes the impairments; the margin path is anchored on the company's underlying figure rebuilt from the segment note, not on the CSV column.
The FX rate converts a USD value to AUD at spot; a 5% move in AUD/USD moves the AUD value 5% with no change in the business.

Method fix: EBITDA margin path restated pre-SBC (+1.1 points in every year and scenario); SBC had been deducted twice

reconciliation.unchanged: Deliberately left alone: all growth paths, SBC %, lease %, capex % and cash-tax paths, WACC 8.5%, terminal growth, the 18x cap, the 25/50/25 weights, the NCI, contingent-consideration and pension bridge items, and the FX rate. The FY2026 annual confirmed every figure they rest on. What would move them: H1 FY2027 results in February 2027 (Behring gross margin, Vifor decline against the 25% guide, working capital), the new chief executive's strategy update, a quantified class-action claim, or a change in US immunoglobulin reimbursement.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted and held FLAT, on the balance-sheet date. 478,911,979 ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 annual report, contributed equity table, CSL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:8608) plus 1,792,284 performance rights and 689,006 performance share units on issue at 31 July 2026 (:12121) = 481.393m. FY2026 reported no dilutive securities only because it was a statutory loss year; the unvested awards are counted here. Shares bought back since 30 June under the A$1.15bn program are NOT removed, and the cash spent on them is NOT deducted: both anchors sit on the same date. SBC is expensed in the flows, so the count is not grown.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings EXCLUDING lease liabilities at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 annual, Note 11): bank 39 + 1,424, senior notes 464 + 2,245, 144A notes 500 + 4,711 = 9,383. Cash 1,513. Lease liabilities of 1,513 (139 + 1,374) are excluded because the lease cost is charged in the flows (treatment B); the Metrics CSV total_debt of 10,896 is the same borrowings INCLUDING leases. The final dividend of US$1.62 a share paid in October 2026 is an ordinary distribution out of FY2027 flows and is not adjusted.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 operating cash flow 3,512 less payments for PPE 646 and intangibles 631 (Metrics CSV; cash flow statement). This figure is LEVERED (after 401 of net finance costs paid) and before 97 of lease principal; it carries about 339 of restructuring cash and about 1,046 of working capital absorbed by receivables, inventories and payables. Unlevered and lease-charged it is about 2,400; adding back restructuring cash after tax gives about 2,700, and the working-capital build explains most of the gap to the model's year-1 flow of about 3,100.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was 30 in FY2026 but the group is in net debt, so no cash pile is added to EV and nothing is stripped.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report (ASX 18 Aug 2026), cash flow statement 'Share-based payment expense' 172 (FY2025: 149). Equity settled; no net-share-settlement tax line in financing, so equity-award taxes are nil.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 payments for share buy-backs 724 (6,406,976 shares, A$1,064m, program completed 5 May 2026). A further A$1.15bn on-market program was announced with the FY2026 result. CSL is a funded repurchaser: buy-backs exceed SBC several times over, so the flat count is paid for.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD; the ASX quote is AUD. All values are computed in USD and converted at USD/AUD 1.4762 (the inverse of Yahoo AUDUSD=X 0.6774, stamped 2026-11-14T10:27Z). Parity check against the Level 1 ADR: CSLLY US$34.41 (close 2026-11-13) x 4 ADS per ordinary share = US$137.64 x 1.4762 = A$203.19 against the ASX close, a 0.13% tie. The 4:1 ratio is confirmed by the dividend (CSLLY US$0.405 against US$1.62 per ordinary share). The rate is not refreshed by price-only updates and must be re-dated whenever the price is.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free about 5.0% (CSL's own 10-year 144A notes priced at 6.201% on 7 October 2026, roughly 110-120bp over Treasuries), equity risk premium 4.75%, beta 0.8 for a defensive plasma franchise: cost of equity about 8.8%. After-tax cost of debt about 4.9%. At roughly 12% debt to enterprise value that is 8.3%, rounded up to 8.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as an operating cost. The FY2026 lease cash cost of 150 (principal 97 in financing plus lease interest 53) is charged every year as 0.95% of revenue through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities of 1,513 are excluded from net debt; and D&A in the tax calculation excludes the 97 of right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. Flows are 100% consolidated (they include Vifor Fresenius Medical Care Renal Pharma, 45% owned by Fresenius Medical Care). The non-controlling interest is deducted at its post-impairment carrying value of 1,510 at 30 June 2026, about 8.5x its FY2026 underlying NPAT share of 177, on a business whose Velphoro and Tavneos revenues are now falling.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios, with the non-US adaptations (USD flows against an AUD quote, IFRS 16 leases, a minority interest). CSL is an operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no bank, REIT or holdco method applies. REBUILD of the same-day first valuation, now that the FY2026 annual report is in the research folder: every anchor was re-read from CSL.AX_Metrics.csv and CSL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt. One method error was found and fixed: the EBITDA margin path had been anchored on underlying EBITDA of 5,282, which is already after the 172 share-based payment expense, and the engine then deducted SBC a second time. The path is now PRE-SBC (FY2026: 5,282 + 172 = 5,454, 34.5% of revenue). See the reconciliation block. PRICE: regular-session ASX close, not an after-hours print; the share price has more than doubled from its 52-week low. EBITDA BASIS: the company's EBITDA of 4,438 (segment note) is statutory EBIT of -3,682 plus D&A 1,041 plus impairments 7,079; adding the 844 of non-impairment restructuring cost gives underlying EBITDA 5,282, which ties to underlying EBIT 4,620 plus D&A excluding acquired IP (555 + 107). The Metrics CSV EBITDA of -2,641 for FY2026 is EBIT plus D&A with the impairments left in and is not a usable margin anchor. EARNINGS ANCHOR: underlying NPATA attributable 3,098 (US$6.43 a share); underlying NPAT attributable 2,837 after 261 of acquired-IP amortisation. Modelled FY2027 NOPAT of about 3,560 less after-tax net finance costs of about 320 and the minority share of about 240 is about 3,000, against guidance of underlying NPAT up about 5% (about 2,980): the flows tie to the guided earnings. NOT MODELLED: the shareholder class action filed 21 October 2026 (unquantified), any further impairments (non-cash), and any Seqirus demerger. A new chief executive, Deborah Waterhouse, starts in February 2027.

base.growth_note: Year 1 is guidance: revenue in line with FY2026 (Behring mid-single-digit at constant currency with immunoglobulin at mid-to-high single digits, Seqirus low-single-digit, Vifor down about 25%). Thereafter Behring (72% of revenue) grows with the immunoglobulin market while Vifor shrinks toward a tenth of the group.
base.margin_note: PRE-SBC underlying EBITDA margin (the engine deducts SBC separately): 34.5% in FY2026 (5,282 + 172 SBC), 34.1% in FY2025, 37.0% at the pre-Vifor peak in FY2021. Year 1 follows guidance of underlying NPAT up about 5%, which rests on cost savings and on lower amortisation after the write-downs rather than on revenue. Later years add the balance of the US$500-550m savings program (part reinvested) and a modest Behring gross-margin recovery from 49.6%, against the loss of Vifor's 70% gross-margin iron revenue.
base.capex_note: Payments for PPE plus intangibles: 8.1% of revenue in FY2026 (646 + 631), 6.4% in FY2025 (636 + 362). The US$1.5bn Kankakee expansion and recurring licence and IP payments keep it at 8.5% for two years before easing to 6.8%.
base.tax_note: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT. Underlying tax expense 879 on underlying pre-tax profit of 4,215 (20.9%) in FY2026, 15.9% in FY2025; cash tax paid was 445, 637 and 784 in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. The start is below the mature rate because deferred tax assets rose from 1,091 to 2,226 with the write-downs; it ramps to 21%.
base.wc_note: Negative: inventories 6,627 plus receivables of about 3,500 less payables 3,475 is about 42% of revenue, so growth consumes cash, and the ratio has been rising: receivables, inventories and payables absorbed 1,046 in FY2026 and 623 in FY2025 on revenue growth of 239 and 758. Capture set at -50% (bull -40%, bear -60%). Year 1 has flat revenue and therefore no working-capital charge, which assumes the FY2026 build does not repeat.
base.da_note: Depreciation and amortisation for the tax calculation, excluding right-of-use depreciation (leases are charged above). FY2026 total 1,041 (PPE and right-of-use 555, acquired IP 379, other intangibles 107), or about 6.0% of revenue excluding roughly 100 of right-of-use depreciation; set at 5.5-5.6% because acquired-IP amortisation falls after 4,845 of intangible impairments.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: management downgraded guidance twice in FY2026 and wrote off US$7.1bn, a new chief executive does not start until February 2027, a class action is on foot, and the core immunoglobulin franchise faces both US pricing reform and FcRn substitution. Base 50%: it is the company's own FY2027 guidance extended at market growth, with the cost program already partly delivered. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires a Behring gross-margin recovery that has been promised since 2022 and not delivered, plus pipeline launches and a Vifor floor, all at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
